action: As the university's notice urges, as reported by Daily SECU: change the passwords of the Hyangrim-tong system and other campus accounts, change any external-site password that was the same, and be wary of smishing and voice phishing impersonating universities, public agencies or financial institutions.
date_note: Day the university's Information and Computing Center issued its apology and notice, per Daily SECU (published 25 November KST); the intrusion date is not stated.
exec: A Korean national university says some users' personal data appears to have leaked from a legacy system; per Boannews, passwords of 6,772 accounts were changed without authorization.
geo_basis: country (article does not state the campus city)
plain: Suncheon National University says it found signs that some users' personal data leaked from its old Hyangrim-tong system. Boannews reports passwords of 6,772 accounts were changed without authorization.
summary: Daily SECU reports that Suncheon National University said on 24 November it detected abnormal external access on its legacy Hyangrim-tong system and found signs that some users' personal data leaked. Boannews reports unauthorized lookups of personal information and that passwords of 6,772 accounts were changed without authorization; the university has not confirmed whether data left the university or how much. The notice says the vulnerability was patched.
title: Suncheon National University says personal data of some users appears to have leaked from legacy Hyangrim-tong system

validation.note: Daily SECU and Boannews (independent publishers) both report the university's 24 November notice of a leak and unauthorized lookups on Hyangrim-tong. The university's own notice page was not read.

review.note: Compared date, notice contents, patch, PIPC and KISA report, undisclosed scale and user advice against Daily SECU
